subject: Fixed-rate lifecycle lock & exit rights — Stello Health
messages:
From: Paul Anderson <paul.anderson@stellohealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: Multi-year pricing: 36-month lock + renewal protections?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. Stello is preparing a three‑year procurement plan and we'd like to explore a fixed-rate, multi‑year arrangement with clear renewal protections. The procurement team has two priorities: a firm price lock for 36 months and an uplift cap on renewal increases (we need predictability for budgeting). We also need an explicit exit/right-to-terminate option in case of major platform regressions or M&A.

Can Redwood provide target language and any typical commercial tradeoffs (e.g., minimum commit, early-exit fees, renewal cap %)? I'm looping our contracting address for records.

Attached: stello_rfp_overview.pdf

Thanks,
Paul Anderson
VP Procurement — Stello Health
paul.anderson@stellohealth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Anderson <paul.anderson@stellohealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing: 36-month lock + renewal protections?

Paul —

Appreciate the clear priorities. High level we can support a 36‑month fixed unit price for token-based usage with an uplift cap on renewals; typical tradeoffs we've seen are higher initial commit or a limited number of renewal protections (e.g., protections for first one or two renewals). Early termination language is negotiable; standard approach is a notice period plus a pre‑paid commitment balance or a sliding exit fee.

I'm going to draft proposed commercial language and escalate to Deal Desk for exec signoff on nonstandard exit fee thresholds. Tentative commercial template attached (stello_redwood_term_sheet_v1.xlsx) and preliminary price sheet (redwood_price_sheet_q1.pdf).

Would you be open to a 10% early-exit fee on remaining committed value if exit occurs before 24 months, and a 60‑day notice? If so, I can table that as the preferred term.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T13:22:00Z
Subject: Escalation: Stello Health — 3yr fixed price + uplift cap + exit rights (DEAL-76831)

Team —

Escalating a request from Stello Health (DEAL-76831). Key asks from the buyer: 36‑month fixed per‑unit price, renewal uplift cap, and an explicit early‑exit right for major regressions / M&A. They are a strategic vertical customer (healthcare) and asking for standard protections plus a 36‑month price lock.

Proposed commercial tradeoffs I'm recommending:
- 36‑month fixed unit price (price lock)
- Renewal uplift cap: 5% annual increase, applied at renewal only
- Early‑exit: 60‑day notice plus 10% of remaining committed spend as exit fee (reduced to 5% if Redwood misses SLA targets for >30 days)
- Minimum annual committed spend: $600k (to offset multi‑year concessions)

Attachments: stello_redwood_term_sheet_v1.xlsx; redwood_price_sheet_q1.pdf
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/76831

Requesting: exec signoff for exception to default renewal protections (we usually limit to first renewal) and approval on early‑exit fee floor.

Let me know if you need alternate scaffolding (e.g., higher commit instead of exit fee).

Thanks,
Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Stello Health — 3yr fixed price + uplift cap + exit rights (DEAL-76831)

Vivek —

Saw Soojin's note. My read: Stello is strategic and the proposed concessions are reasonable if we protect economics. A few redline suggestions for approval:
- Keep minimum commit at $600k/year but require a 50% non‑refundable upfront payment in year 1 for customer to get full 36‑month lock. This effectively hedges our tail risk.
- Renewal uplift cap at 5% annually, but cap cumulative uplift over the full term to 12% (prevents step jumps).
- Early‑exit fee: keep 10% of remaining committed value; add SLA reduction clause (as Soojin proposed) to lower fee to 5% if we materially breach uptime SLA for >30 days.

I've attached a marked-up term sheet (stello_redwood_term_sheet_v1.xlsx — redlines). If you'd authorize the above, legal (cc'd: laura_bennett) can turn this into final contract language and ops can set up reporting to track SLA triggers.

Marissa
VP Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Stello Health — 3yr fixed price + uplift cap + exit rights (DEAL-76831)

Ok to approve with the following conditions (records):
1) Minimum annual commitment remains $600k with 50% non‑refundable upfront in year 1.
2) Renewal uplift cap: 5% per year; cumulative uplift over term <= 12%.
3) Early‑exit: 60‑day notice plus 10% exit fee on remaining committed value; reduce to 5% if Redwood experiences SLA failure >30 days as documented by ops.
4) Legal to confirm final contract wording on 'material regression' definition and SLA measurement method (Laura).

Marissa/Soojin: proceed to finalize term sheet and send to Stello with docuSign link. Ops/legal, please stand by for implementation items.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer — Redwood Inference
